item.title: OBP tells Parliament it’s still behind on GMP project
item.description: Onderstepoort Biological Productsis struggling to find a suitable specialist adviser to assist with its project to improve manufacturing standards, Parliament has heard. OBP also reported a loss for the first two quarters of the financial year.

item.title: How Agri Skills Transfer is preparing a new generation for Africa’s agricultural future
item.description: As the agriculture industry is called upon to produce more with fewer resources, the Cullinan campus of Agri Skills Transfer is continuing to grow the skills necessary for sustainable agriculture and future rural development in South Africa.

item.title: FMD | Dunevax places confidence in state and delivers vaccines to OBP
item.description: As South Africa races to contain foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), another shipment of vaccines have now been delivered to Onderstepoort Biological Products (OBP). Yet reports of poor traceability in the field, shortages of equipment and questions about payment for the shipment are raising fresh concerns among farmers and industry stakeholders.

item.title: SA Ceres Fruit Growers claims global food safety honour
item.description: In a testament to unwavering commitment to food safety excellence, Ceres Fruit Growers (CFG) has been named BRCGS Certificated Site of the Year 2026, receiving this prestigious global recognition in London. The award celebrates the South African company’s exceptional standards in food safety, quality management and supply chain integrity.

item.title: High average for All-in-One Crux’s Dohne Merino sheep
item.description: The award-winning Dohne-Merino stud All-in-One Crux of Wikus Bekker at Edenburg can boast relatively high average prices and a 100% sale rate at the stud's 22nd production sale on 5 February 2026.

item.title: FMD in piggeries: Cases increase but approvals for designated abattoirs still slow
item.description: The South African Pork Producers’ Organisation (SAPPO) began reporting outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in the country’s commercial piggeries from November last year. Latest figures show that confirmed or suspected cases of FMD in such piggeries since then increased from seven in early February to 10 a month later. Although some piggeries have since recovered from their infections, there are reportedly still too few abattoirs approved to slaughter their animals.

item.title: WATCH | Bodibe communal farmers vaccinate to increase cattle market value
item.description: Bodibe Village in Ditsobotla Local Municipality witnessed a groundbreaking two-day livestock vaccination campaign on 25 and 26 February as communal farmers took decisive action to address the chronic problem of poor cattle auction prices as a result of disease concerns.

item.title: WATCH | Government ramps up FMD vaccination campaign in Gauteng
item.description: John Steenhuisen, the Minister of Agriculture, and Vuyiswa Ramokgopa, the Gauteng MEC for Agriculture and Rural Development (GDARD), led a ministerial foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccination outreach campaign in Katlehong on the East Rand, Johannesburg, today. During this event, over 200 cattle were vaccinated and tagged as part of the government’s intensified response to FMD.

item.title: Strong demand for Gras Karoo Dormers
item.description: Enthusiastic bidding from the present buyers and on the SwiftVEE platform was an indication of the demand for quality Dormers at the annual production auction of Gras Karoo Dormers from the farm Venterskraal, Venterstad district, on 18 February 2026.
